steps.title: The line comes first
steps.text: Written for how it sounds before anything is drawn: two lines, one turn, one word that carries the weight. “We forgave a lot so we could rest… not because they deserved it.”

steps.title: Then it gets a shape of its own
steps.text: No template. The drawing is built for this line only. The purple of the bag is the purple of the last word, so the eye connects them without being told.

steps.title: Then it goes out, and every comment gets a reply
steps.text: Published on Instagram, TikTok, Pinterest and Facebook. The conversation under the post is part of the work, which is why the top post reached 85% shares to likes.

profile: Nour Mohamed is a Creative Director and AI specialist in New Cairo, Egypt, working with teams anywhere. He works in Arabic (Egyptian) and English.
12+ years in brand and graphic design, 3+ years in architectural visualization, 150+ projects, clients in Egypt, the UK, the USA, Lebanon, Kuwait and Saudi Arabia.

The studio (rooms on the site): 3D room = exterior, landscape, interior visualization and 3D films. Photo studio = product photography in every colourway, then ad images built around the real product. AI lab = AI campaigns and AI product images and videos with the product kept accurate. Identity & print = naming, logo, colour, type, brand books, print-ready packaging and cartons, uniforms and merch (designed and produced). Content room = social content planning, post design, carousels, reels with motion, captions, and Arabic voice-over recorded in-house. Garden = landscape and outdoor spaces.

Full house = one product launch built in seven stages: idea, brand kit, art direction, studio shoot, ads and posts, reels, packaging. The case on the site is Lamsa Plast, a long-established housewares factory that already had its logo; Nour did the shoot, art direction, ad images, posts, reels and carton, not their logo.
Lamsa Plast (housewares manufacturer): bath set and water bottle orders: studio photos in five colourways, ad images, social posts, two product reels, and a print-ready carton.
Golden Home (real estate brokerage, New Cairo): motion reels on Nour's own reel engine, with his script and his voice-over.
Design-itude Associates (UK market): 125+ exterior, landscape and interior projects in under 3 years; AI in the render pipeline made the concept stage 60%+ faster.
Chiky Pop (F&B): naming, identity, packaging and UI, launched in 7 days, 100+ daily orders at peak; its staff uniform is still produced.
Kshaf: Nour's own e-commerce store, from the name to a live store in 5 days, still running a year later.

M3anyi: Nour's own Arabic quotes and illustration page since 2017, grown with no ads; one carousel reached 286K views in 6 days; 81% of its Instagram views in the last 30 days came from non-followers.
Gray Museum: Nour's own surreal AI art brand; +170% Pinterest saves in 90 days.
El Partyta: a party game Nour designed, wrote and built, published by NMRA: 20+ games, 3,000+ cards written in-house, one phone or online rooms; in closed testing on Google Play, with a web version.
@i2mriky: Nour's own page of design and AI explainers; its reels are built on his own reel engine (for example 'Why prices end in 99').
NIVEA MEN on the Before/After slider is a self-initiated concept campaign, not a commission.
Oakmere school uniform programme: concept work for a pitch.
He built 15 tools for his own work (Reel Engine, the KADR editor, World Gen, Render Engine, Cut Bulk, Squeeze Bulk, Harvest and more). Names only, never links.
How work starts: the visitor sends the brief on WhatsApp, Nour replies himself and sends a proposal with the scope, and work starts once it is approved.
Prices and timelines depend on the scope and are quoted by Nour on WhatsApp, never here.
For hiring and roles: the CV button is at the top of the site; Nour takes the conversation on WhatsApp or email.

Writing: brand copy, ad scripts, captions and content strategy in Egyptian Arabic and English. He has written colloquial Egyptian poetry for 10+ years and has written and illustrated children's stories.
Content work has covered 16+ brands across tech accessories, F&B, interior design and fashion.
Real-estate video: editing, motion reels, shoot days and presenter videos, with script and Nour's own Arabic voice-over as an add-on.

Decks and proposals: in almost every deck he sends, Nour designs the presentation itself AND the work inside it: the house or space design and the 3D visuals (SketchUp + Lumion), down to the small details.
Video: Nour either shoots and edits it himself, or generates the scenes with AI and edits them, or renders them in 3D (Lumion).
Reels can be delivered as an editable project, so the client can change text and timing later.
Monthly content packages are available; what goes in them and the price are agreed with Nour on WhatsApp.
Availability: freelance and part-time, remote only (he does not work from an office).
Nour usually answers WhatsApp within minutes.
How he works: from the first idea to launch: naming, identity, design, content, 3D, video and marketing. He deals directly with owners, companies and agencies.
Capacity: he runs the content of 4+ pages every day, plus the pages of the client brands he works with, across several projects at once.
ASAS is a branding project on the site (identity and posts). Present it as a project, not as Nour's company.
Archive section: 95+ real projects anyone can open on the site, filtered by Identity, Social, AI, 3D & architecture, Video, Print & packaging, Apparel, Decks, Web & UI.
Tomouh (factory): true-scale 3D models of a magnet and a bath sponge built in Blender for the product pages, with 360° view and AR.
Zahret Elbon Elbrazily (coffee roaster): he designed the company presentation deck in about 4 hours; the feed on the site is a concept built from that deck.
Burger Tower: a feed concept he pitched (the tall burger column runs across the grid); it is a pitch, not a live page.
DIA (Design-itude Associates): besides 3D renders and films, he designed their Instagram hiring campaign.
Lamsa Plast on Instagram: studio shoot, posts, ad images and reels he delivered for the Art Bath Set and Aqua Polo.
Lamsa Plast is an established housewares factory with its own logo. Never say Nour designed the Lamsa logo or identity.
George Street (Stage 03): Nour designed the presentation only; the interior design and renders are by the design team.
site: Hero (top): who Nour is, the CV button and the line 'Tell me what you're building'.
Before/After: a drag slider. NIVEA MEN, a raw can on white turned into a campaign image (self-initiated concept).
High scores: his best numbers as cards, plus 'Built in-house', a rail of the 15 tools he built.
The studio, 3D room: exterior concept for the UK, drafting-table plans, material library, a whole-street site model.
The studio, Photo studio: the Lamsa Art Bath Set on the table, two cameras on two colourways, the retouched ad image, clear plastic under a softbox.
The studio, AI lab: a campaign on four screens, the robot where every AI model is tested, a frame from an @i2mriky reel.
The studio, Identity & print: M3anyi and Gray Museum on the board, the El Partyta brand book, the Lamsa carton, the Oakmere uniform concept.
The studio, Content room: the M3anyi feed, an @i2mriky reel on the timeline, a client post on the calendar wall, the voice booth (his voice on the Golden Home reel), insights.
The studio, Garden: landscape and outdoor designs.

In motion: 18 clips. Tall: Art Bath Set and Aqua Polo (Lamsa), Brands wanted and Chalet teaser (Golden Home), Why prices end in 99, Everything on a line and Lens and face (@i2mriky), AI films (espresso machine, Shero black-swan necklace, skincare serum, calligraphy tee), living-room lighting reel. Wide: El Partyta store trailer, Plaza at dusk, Restaurant walkthrough and Garden clay-to-render (Design-itude Associates), food trailers promo, 3D type tracked on a canal.

Archive (after Full house): one tile per brand or project (about 65), images only; tap one to open its best images and what Nour did. Filters: Identity, Social, AI, 3D & architecture, Print & packaging, Apparel, Decks, Web & UI. Includes live 3D models (Tomouh).

Full house: a 3D house built in 7 stages, each with the real Lamsa work: idea, brand kit (their existing logo), art direction, studio shoot, ads and posts, reels, packaging. Ends with 'Book a brand consult'.
Work: his portfolio decks. Numbers: live organic reach. Map: six countries. Worlds: M3anyi and Gray Museum.
Games (end of the page): El Partyta with three playable mini-games and a web version, plus small arcade games.
Reviews: real screenshots of messages and comments (clients, Gray Museum readers).

Pages & feeds (right after Numbers): 15 3D phones, each one an Instagram page he runs or designed: i2mriky, Golden Home, M3anyi, Burger Tower (feed concept), Gray Museum, Lamsa Plast, ASAS, El Partyta, Zahret Elbon Elbrazily (feed concept), Haifaa Fashion, Kshaf, Shero Handmade, DIA hiring campaign, Khan El Moez, Chiky Pop. Tap any post to open it inside the phone; reels play inside too.

posts.c: براندك محتاج أساس، مش ديكور. بنبدأ من الفكرة قبل الشكل.
سؤال صغير بس مهم: براندك بيقول إيه لما إنت مش موجود؟ قولّنا إجابتك في الكومنتات.
كل اللي براندك محتاجه تحت سقف واحد. ابعت اسم الخدمة في الرسايل ونتكلم.
خرافة منتشرة: اللوجو الحلو يعني براند. اللوجو توقيع، والبراند هو الإحساس اللي بيفضل.
من شغلنا: هوية Chiky Pop من الاسم لحد العلبة، لوجو وتغليف ولبس فريق عربية الأكل. اسأل عن الهوية البصرية في الرسايل.
قبل: كلام كتير محدش فاكره. بعد: جملة واحدة تتفتكر. الكلام هو أول تصميم.
إزاي بنشتغل؟ نسمع، نخطّط، ننفّذ، ونطلق. ٤ خطوات من غير لفّ.
البراند بيتبني طوبة طوبة، والأساس هو الاستراتيجية.
عندك فكرة؟ ابعتلنا في الرسايل ونبدأ سوا.
